sources.title: Demkowicz and Gopalakrishnan, Analysis of the DPG method for the Poisson equation
sources.actual_read_extent_this_cycle: Introduction and abstract framework; explicit initial domain hypothesis (text lines 184–185); complete Sections 4.1–4.3 through Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 4.2 proof opening/decomposition and estimates through text line 1100. Not a claim to have read the entire 22-page paper this cycle.
sources.exact_disposition: Domain is bounded simply connected with connected Lipschitz boundary. Lemma 4.3 obtains a vector potential by the exact-sequence property under its topological assumptions. This route does not supply the desired connected-domain proof. Proposed proof uses no Lemma 4.3, Hodge or potential representation.

sources.title: Gopalakrishnan and Qiu, An analysis of the practical DPG method
sources.actual_read_extent_this_cycle: Complete Sections 1–2 including Theorem 2.1 proof; complete Sections 3.1–3.4 through Lemmas 3.1–3.3 full proofs and Theorem 3.4 statement (text lines 1–800). Linear elasticity section not read this cycle.
sources.exact_disposition: Exact real product graph norms, global extension quotient norms, and the signed form agree literally with local formulation. Model inf-sup is imported from the prior source. General scalar test degree r>=p+N yields r=3 at p=1,N=2; no tetrahedral scalar R3 conclusion is supplied. New arbitrary-dual-load lifting is locally derived, not asserted to be their proof.

sources.title: Carstensen, Demkowicz and Gopalakrishnan, A Posteriori Error Control for DPG Methods
sources.actual_read_extent_this_cycle: Complete Theorem 2.1, Remarks 2.2–2.6 and its complete proof; Section 3.1 through Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 3.2 statement (text lines 240–565). Not a claim to have read the whole 21-page paper this cycle.
sources.exact_disposition: Orthogonal residual decomposition and oscillation estimates match the actual local conditional theorem. Poisson application cites original ideal/practical sources; it does not replace the local topology-free proof obligation. Its generic scalar degree is p+N.
